title: Data Quality & Schema Evolution
interviewAnswer: Production pipelines should validate schema, ranges, null rates, uniqueness and business constraints. Schema changes need explicit compatibility and migration strategies rather than silent breakage.
why: Models depend on upstream data contracts; schema or distribution failures can break predictions even when model code is unchanged.
intuition: Data quality means the data is structurally valid and semantically plausible for the intended use: correct schema, ranges, completeness, uniqueness and freshness.
deepDive: Schema evolution includes added/removed columns, type changes and semantic changes that a schema alone may not detect. Define expectations for null rate, uniqueness, ranges, category sets, row counts and freshness. Some changes are backward compatible; others require coordinated producer/consumer rollout. Data validation should occur at ingestion and before training/inference.
workedExample: If a temperature column changes from Celsius to Fahrenheit while keeping the same numeric type/name, schema validation passes but semantic distribution checks should flag the shift.
commonMistakes: Rejecting every new category/schema addition without compatibility rules.
Monitoring model performance but not upstream freshness/null rates.
followUps: How handle a new categorical value?
How do you roll out schema changes safely?
production: Use contracts, lineage, freshness SLOs, quarantine for bad batches and alerts that identify the upstream source before downstream models fail.
